description: Spouting off before listening to the facts is both shameful and foolish. This reads like it was written for the exact culture we are living in.
excerpt: We post before we research. We repost before we read the article. We form strong opinions in about four seconds and then broadcast them to everyone we know. And Proverbs calls it what it is. Foolish.
verse: "Spouting off before listening to the facts is both shameful and foolish."
body_html:
This is another one of those verses that reads like it was written for the exact culture we are living in.

We spout off constantly. We post before we research. We repost before we read the article. We share the meme without checking if any of it is even true. We comment on things we do not actually understand. We form strong opinions in about four seconds and then broadcast them to everyone we know.

And Proverbs calls it what it is. Foolish.

Not just unwise. Not just a bad habit. Shameful and foolish.

That word shameful is important because we do not really think of it that way anymore. We have made a whole culture out of quick takes and strong reactions. We reward the loudest voices, not the most thoughtful ones. Being the first to comment feels more important than being the most informed.

But God is not impressed with how fast we can talk.

It shows up in our personal conversations too. How often are we actually listening when someone is talking to us? Or are we just waiting for our turn to share what we already think? Are we asking questions to learn, or asking them to steer the conversation to what we want to say next?

Real listening is rare. And it is one of the most Christ-like things a person can do.

Jesus asked questions constantly. He let people talk. He listened. He drew things out of them. He did not rush to correct or fix or explain. He was fully present in conversations in a way most of us are not, because our minds are already three steps ahead planning our response.

The hard part is that this verse is convicting for me. Because I do this too. I have opinions. I want to share them. I can spout off with the best of them if I am not careful. And every time I do, I usually regret it. Not because I was wrong, necessarily, but because I skipped the listening part.

Listening first is humility. Talking first is pride.

That is really what this verse is about. It is one more reminder that in a world that rewards volume, God still rewards wisdom. And wisdom takes its time. It hears the whole story. It asks questions. It considers. It waits before it speaks.

I want to be more of that kind of person. Slower to post. Slower to comment. Slower to share the take. Faster to listen and consider and understand before I ever open my mouth.
question: Where in your life have you been spouting off when God is inviting you to listen first?
